decisions.question: navigation-api@v1 G13 fixes the nav-resolver's edges and order but not the functions they record; topology-ir@v1 G9 leaves a closure anonymous. Should the template's two stage functions be closures or named method tear-offs?

options.label: method tear-offs of private stage classes
options.consequence: The recorded IR and every rendered graph name the stages resolveDeepLinks and applyAuthGuard, as Guide §3.4 draws them; about 35 more lines; consumers can see the names, so a compatible amend of G13 goes to reconcile and hsdd-contract adds an assertion or a not-executable line.

options.label: closures
options.consequence: No extra code and no amend, but two of the resolver's three transforms render as (anonymous) in bus.toGraph(), the catalog and the JSON form.

decisions.chosen: method tear-offs of private stage classes
decisions.why: Spec §6.2 asks for named transformers and Spec §6.5 treats a topology as self-documenting data; the experiment shows tear-offs record the names in both forms, keep two resolvers of one configuration equal, and pass all 40 navigation cases and 52 executor registrations unchanged. Because the names are visible across the boundary the choice is emitted as an amend rather than kept node-local.

decisions.question: How to cut nidana.navigation into phases under fp-progression: where the resolver template and resultsFor go, and whether the in-memory router stands alone.

options.label: six phases, template with the guard
options.consequence: Declarations; values; access, guard and resolver template (full-review, ~400 lines); executor values and planner; in-memory router; executor and live wiring. The security chain (guard table plus resolve-before-guard order) is reviewed in one sitting; the guard work waits on nidana.model.11 for its G13 replay.

options.label: seven phases, template in its own phase
options.consequence: A spot-check template phase of about 180 lines that could run beside the values and planner lanes as soon as nidana.model.11 merges; one more cycle whose process artifacts would rival its diff, and the guard and the stage order reviewed apart.

options.label: five phases, router folded into the planner
options.consequence: One cycle fewer, but the merged phase comes to about 500 lines, over the review window, and mixes the pure band with the effect band.

decisions.chosen: six phases, template with the guard
decisions.why: The template alone sits below the sizing floor, and the guard and the template's stage order together are one security property (navigation-api@v1 Refinement 3), so reviewing them together in one full-review phase buys more than the parallel lane. resultsFor rides with the template because both are recorded DSL compositions. The signal that would have favored seven phases: nidana.model.11 expected to land much later than nidana.model.8, holding up the guard work.

decisions.question: Review tier of nidana.navigation.3 (access values, resolveDeepLinks, applyAuthGuard, navResolver, resultsFor), a mostly pure phase.

options.label: full-review
options.consequence: A full design and verification doc and a diff read for a pure phase; the guard table and the stage order get edge-case review.

options.label: spot-check
options.consequence: Cheaper review of well-constrained pure functions with exhaustive fixture cases; a subtle guard or order error relies on the fixtures alone.

decisions.why: The phase decides access: an error in G12's table or in the template's stage order opens a protected route, the bypass navigation-api@v1 Refinement 3 exists to close. The tier table puts security at full-review.

decisions.question: Where do the live resolver replays (G14, G16) land: with the resolver template, or in the final phase with the executor?

options.label: final phase
options.consequence: The template phase stays pure and waits on nothing later than nidana.model.11; G14 and G16 replay once, at nidana.navigation.6, which waits on nidana.runtime.14 anyway.

options.label: with the template
options.consequence: The template phase would wait on nidana.runtime.14, the hard edge, putting a pure phase on the critical path after the runtime ships.

decisions.why: --guarantee selects by guarantee id, and G16 has one recorded and one live case, so G16 cannot replay before a real TestBus exists; G14 is all live. The template adds no code for live behavior, which is the runtime's interpretation of the recorded plan. Keeping nidana.navigation.1 to .5 off nidana.runtime.14 lets them merge while the runtime's later phases run.
evidence: ADR-001 item 9 (--guarantee restricts behavior cases by name prefix)

decisions.question: Which phase replays G9 (the five topic declarations, complete at nidana.navigation.1), whose case needs topic-model@v1's values from nidana.model.8?

options.label: nidana.navigation.3
options.consequence: nidana.navigation.2 starts after nidana.model.6 alone; nidana.navigation.3 already needs nidana.model.8 for G13's TopicRef comparisons.

options.label: nidana.navigation.2
options.consequence: The topics replay one phase earlier, but nidana.navigation.2 and everything after it wait on nidana.model.8.

decisions.why: It removes a cross-node wait from nidana.navigation.2 at no cost, since nidana.navigation.3 depends on nidana.model.8 for G13 regardless.
evidence: topic-model@v1 Delivery (nidana.model.8 delivers every behavior guarantee)

decisions.question: Should the executor and the live composition (G14, G15, G16, G24 and the bootstrap test) be one phase or two?

options.label: one phase
options.consequence: About 360 lines (100 of library code), 7 plan tasks, full-review; nidana.flutter's binding of the executor suite waits on one phase.

options.label: two phases
options.consequence: An executor phase and a live-wiring phase that writes almost no library code; the second's process artifacts would exceed its diff, and flutter's G24 replay would wait on a later phase than G18 to G23.

decisions.why: The composition writes tests, not code, and the executor's G19 to G24 cases already exercise the bus wiring; split, the second phase sits below the floor with the same tier and contracts as the first.

decisions.question: What does nidana.navigation.1, the type-level phase, land beyond signatures: constructors, consts, equality? (D1)

options.label: copying constructors, bodies throw
options.consequence: Constructors assign fields and copy collections, consts are whole, every other computing body throws UnimplementedError and equality stays Object's; G4 replays from nidana.navigation.2; consumers on nidana.navigation.1 can construct values but compare by identity.

options.label: value equality in phase 1
options.consequence: About 250 more lines in a phase already over the PE target, and G5 to G8 split across two phases.

options.label: throwing constructors
options.consequence: G4 waits for nidana.navigation.4 and RouteState is unusable in nidana.navigation.3's tests.

decisions.why: ADR-001 item 10 needs every declaration in the first producing phase; field assignment and copying are the declarations' shape, and the reject codes were confirmed against final fields. The schedule reaches consumers through the Delivery sub-bullets.
evidence: nidana.model D3 (the same choice for nidana_dart_contracts)

decisions.question: Source layout of nidana_dart_navigation below its two public libraries (D2).

options.label: one library per area
options.consequence: Phases that run side by side edit disjoint files, so no phase collides; routes and intents share one library because NavRoute builds GoTo, Replace and ShowModal through private constructors.

options.label: one library with part files
options.consequence: Matches the stand-in, but nidana.navigation.3 and .4 would edit one library and serialize behind Collides with.

decisions.why: It keeps the parallel lane after nidana.navigation.2 real and leaves no Collides with entries in the plan.

decisions.question: At nidana.navigation.2 to .5 the --guarantee restriction admits no case of in_memory_router_test.dart (the executor suite, G18 to G24). Can those gates replay behavior at all? (D3)

options.label: replay restricted, relying on nidana.model D2
options.consequence: Pure guarantees replay as they land; the executor binding passes with no case run, which nidana.model D2 items 1 and 4 imply and nidana.runtime's gates already rely on for bus_activation_test.dart.

options.label: surface and reject only until nidana.navigation.6
options.consequence: No reliance on the empty-binding reading, but G1, G4 to G13, G17 and G25 would go unreplayed until the last phase.

decisions.chosen: replay restricted, relying on nidana.model D2
decisions.why: The same reading was accepted at S31 (DEC-461) for nidana.runtime's gates; dart test's exit 79 on an empty filter is a hazard for the tool's implementation, not for the plan. The signal that would change this: nidana.model.6 stating that a binding whose filter admits no case fails.

decisions.question: How do this node's gates check navigation-api@v1 G26 and G27, which the contract marks not executable? (D4)

options.label: a package properties test
options.consequence: test/package_properties_test.dart runs under fvm dart test in every gate: dependencies, imports, forbidden clock, timer and microtask calls, and sync: true controllers.

options.label: a search in the gate
options.consequence: Not an fvm command and outside the package's tests.

decisions.why: Gates stay fvm commands, and the check runs with the package's tests at every phase, as nidana.model D6 and nidana.runtime D9 do for their packages. The sync: true clause was added because an asynchronous StreamController schedules a microtask per event, which G27 forbids.

decisions.question: What does NavigationExecutor do when a router violates G18 (a perform that throws, an error event on confirmations), and is that a contract matter? (D6)

options.label: no handling, node-local
options.consequence: A perform's throw reaches the provider zone's handler through bus-api@v1 G18 and later intents are still handled; a confirmations error reaches the constructor zone's handler and the subscription continues; no declaration or amend.

options.label: catch and report a new ShellDiagnostic
options.consequence: Compatible under Versioning, but a declaration and fixture work for a path no conforming router reaches.

options.label: amend G20 stating the propagation
options.consequence: Consumers could rely on it, at the cost of a guarantee clause and a fixture case for router defects.

decisions.why: No conforming router produces either event, so no consumer relies on the behavior; Dart's own unhandled-error path is where a router's author looks. The signal that would change this: a platform router that throws from perform by design, such as a Flutter router before it is hosted, which flutter-binding@v1 Refinement 2 rules out.

decisions.question: nidana.navigation.1 comes to about 500 lines, over the ~400-line PE target. Split it or accept it?

options.label: accept, gate-only
options.consequence: One review sitting over declarations transcribed from the Interface; surface and reject pass in full from it.

options.label: split off a package-scaffold phase
options.consequence: A non-producing phase of about 100 lines below the floor; the declarations cannot split further because ADR-001 item 10 runs surface and reject in full from the first producing phase.

decisions.why: Splitting removes only scaffolding and the properties test while adding a cycle; the declarations themselves must land together. Recorded as a sizing note under the summary table.

decisions.question: Which phases does the confirm entry list as consumers of bus-testing@v1 and topology-ir@v1, given that every behavior replay compiles conformance libraries importing testing.dart and topology_ir.dart?

options.label: phases that use them
options.consequence: bus-testing@v1: nidana.navigation.6 only (the hard edge); topology-ir@v1: nidana.navigation.3 and .6, whose gates replay the cases naming its declarations; compile-only needs are covered by nidana.navigation.1's waits on nidana.runtime.1 and nidana.model.5.

options.label: every phase that compiles them
options.consequence: Lists nidana.navigation.2 to .5 as bus-testing@v1 consumers, which under the root DAG's hard typing would read as waiting on nidana.runtime.14.

decisions.why: The root DAG types runtime to navigation as hard for bus-testing@v1, and the orchestrator asked topology-ir@v1 to be listed in the phases whose gates replay G13, G15, G16, G19 and G24; the sub-bullets record the compile-only reach so reconcile does not lose it.

experiments.question: S1: which FunctionRefs does the recorded nav-resolver carry with closure stages versus method tear-offs of private stage classes? S2: do navigation-api@v1's two bindings, from the repository's fixtures, still pass with named stages? S3: what does an error event on a synchronous broadcast stream do to a listener that passes onData only?
experiments.finding: S1: closures record FunctionRef.anonymous() for the intent map and the withLatestFrom in both forms; tear-offs record resolveDeepLinks and applyAuthGuard; the auth map records principalOf either way; two resolvers of one configuration record equal definitions in every case. S2: the navigation suite passes 40/40 and the executor suite 52/52 on InMemoryRouter with closures and with tear-offs. S3: the error reaches the listening zone's uncaught-error handler and the subscription keeps receiving later events.

Governance, amend (compatible): navigation-api@v1 G13 gains the stage functions' names (resolveDeepLinks, applyAuthGuard, FunctionRef.of(principalOf)). Reconcile should route a fixture assertion on G13's first case through hsdd-contract, or add a not-executable line for the clause (ADR-001 item 3). Governance, request: none. No gap was found in topic-model@v1, topology-dsl@v1, topology-ir@v1, bus-api@v1 or bus-testing@v1 that this plan needs answered.

Routed items: OQ-N1 and OQ-N2 marked RESOLVED (2026-10-18) with detail paragraphs; consumed contracts' Delivery paragraphs read and cited in each confirm (nidana.model.5/.8/.9/.10/.11/.12, nidana.runtime.1/.14); topology-ir@v1 listed in the phases replaying G13 (nidana.navigation.3) and G15, G16, G19, G24 (nidana.navigation.6); the executor suite on InMemoryRouter and the navigation suite run in this node's gates, flutter's binding does not (D3).

Node-local decisions recorded in the spec: D1 what nidana.navigation.1 lands; D2 source layout (no Collides with in the plan); D3 what every gate runs; D4 G26/G27 properties test; D5 named stage functions; D6 no executor error handling.

For later plans: nidana.flutter's phase that binds the executor suite to FlutterNavigationExecutor waits on nidana.navigation.6 (its cases construct NavigationExecutor; G24 also runs navResolver live); its contract edge for compiling against navigation-api@v1 waits on nidana.navigation.1. nidana.tooling's edges on navigation-api@v1 are names only and wait on nidana.navigation.1. nidana.integration's hard edge waits on nidana.navigation.6. Values compare by identity until nidana.navigation.2 (routes, intents, RouteState), .3 (access values) and .4 (executor values).
